ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, and signatories against the UN Security Council consolidated list, the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions list, the Swiss Embargo Act (SR 946.2), the OFAC SDN list, EU restrictive measures where applicable, and INTERPOL/NCB references. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must receive enhanced due diligence including documented source of wealth, source of funds, higher approval authority, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Screening is repeated on a quarterly basis and triggered by material ownership or registry changes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Names Index (https://www.zefix.ch) and the competent cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce / Ufficio del registro di commercio)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names are registered in the official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian or Romansh) in Latin script; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into an official language. The legal suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or its abbreviation 'AG' or 'SA' must be used. The name must be distinctive, truthful, not misleading, and must not improperly suggest a connection with the Confederation, a canton, a municipality, or a regulated financial activity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss / Schweiz / Suisse (when implying state sponsorship)
Cantonal or municipal names requiring authority consent (e.g., Zurich, Zug, Geneva)
Public authority or public office references
Terms suggesting regulated investment or securities activity without a licence
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the cantonal Commercial Register Office within 30 days of the written rejection notice, specifying the grounds of distinctiveness and non-deceptiveness. If the register office sustains the rejection, a second-level appeal is available to the cantonal administrative court or the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority. An expiring reservation may be renewed by filing a fresh name-clearance application before the original reservation lapses; the renewal is subject to the applicable statutory filing fee and a further Zefix conflict search.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is accepted only as a registered correspondence address where a physical Swiss office with service-of-process capability, document custody, and administrative substance is separately maintained. For ISIC 6209 data-center colocation leasing, the registered office should coincide with a genuine administrative or operational Swiss address, such as the data-center management office; a pure virtual letterbox without local substance will be rejected by the commercial register and may trigger involuntary dissolution procedures.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated at 20% ± 10% in the first 18 months post-incorporation for a foreign-owned Swiss AG in data-center colocation. Cantonal commercial register, cantonal tax administration, social security equalization funds, and FINMA/SECO officers retain the right to conduct unannounced inspections. The probability rises materially where the registered address is a virtual office, the UBO structure is non-transparent, or cross-border equipment leasing triggers VAT/customs audit triggers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Articles 620-763 governing the Aktiengesellschaft (AG/S.A.); Federal Ordinance on the Commercial Register (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV), Articles 5-18 and 93-97.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug / Registre du commerce du canton de Zoug), acting under federal supervision of the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Section (Eidg. Amt für das Handelsregister) and published through the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation together with the Articles of Association (Statuten) and the Commercial Register application (Anmeldung zum Handelsregister) submitted electronically via the notary through the federal e-register platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of CHF 100,000, fully subscribed at incorporation; at least 20% of each subscribed share's par value, with aggregate paid-in cash not below CHF 50,000, must be deposited into a bank blocked account in the name of the future company, and the bank's blocking confirmation (Bestätigung nach Art. 632 Abs. 3 OR) must be annexed to the deed; funds remain escrowed until the Commercial Register entry, unless replaced by a qualified contribution-in-kind report (Sacheinlagebericht).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporation deed and Articles of Association be and hereby are approved; that the par-value capital of CHF 100,000 divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 each be subscribed and allotted to the founding shareholders, and the bank confirmation under Art. 632 para. 3 of the Swiss Code of Obligations be accepted as proof of payment; that the registered office of the Company be established at [address], Canton of Zug; that [Name], [Name], and [Name] be appointed respectively Chairman of the Board, Chief Executive Officer with sole signature, and Company Secretary; and that the officers be and hereby are authorized to execute all filings, permit applications, and lease and construction documents for the data-center colocation business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription and Swiss Blocked-Account Confirmation (Libra-Bestätigung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank or Swiss branch of a foreign bank (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank or an authorized private bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a specially blocked bank account (Libra-Konto) in the exact name of the intended Aktiengesellschaft; transfer from the founding shareholders at least CHF 50,000 of the CHF 100,000 par capital; instruct the bank to issue a written capital-blocking confirmation addressed to the notary and the future company; the confirmation remains valid only while the funds are irrevocably blocked until Commercial Register registration.
required_dossiers: Founders' passports or national identity documents
Source-of-funds declaration and bank account opening forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the blocking instruction, correct the payment reference or provide a revised confirmation; if the bank refuses, select an alternate licensed bank and re-open the blocked account; a contribution-in-kind valuation report may substitute for cash-only payment where lawful.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Deed of Incorporation and Adoption of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Canton of Zug (Notariat des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All incorporators appear personally or by power of attorney before the notary; the notary verifies identity, reads and certifies the Deed of Incorporation, confirms receipt of the capital-blocking certificate and, where applicable, the contribution-in-kind report; the deed contains the Articles of Association, subscription of all shares, appointment of the first board and signatories, and the registered office; amend any defects at the notary's instruction before signature is fully effective.
required_dossiers: Contribution-in-kind and audit report, if any
Written power of attorney for any deponent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires modifications, execute an addendum or a fresh deed at the same notary's office; unresolved defects such as insufficient paid-in capital must be cured by an additional blocked deposit before re-execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Application and Legal Compliance Review (Handelsregisteranmeldung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug, filed electronically by the notary via the federal e-register platform (eGR) of the Federal Commercial Register Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the registration application together with the certified deed, Articles of Association, the list of board members and authorized signatories (with exact signature modalities), declarations of consent of each officer, and the verification of the registered office address at a physically tenable location in Canton Zug; register the option for the auditor waiver (Art. 727a OR) if the statutory requirements are met; upon verification of substantive and formal compliance, the Commercial Register enters the company; legal personality commences with entry.
required_dossiers: List of board members and officers with nationality and residence
Auditor waiver declaration (Art. 727a OR), if applicable
Bank confirmation of fully subscribed and paid capital
Proof of registered office address in Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register officer issues a deficiency notice (Mängelrüge), all defects may be cured within 30 calendar days, with one possible extension of 30 days upon a reasoned request; if not cured the application is dismissed without prejudice and a new filing can be made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Entry in Zefix, Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce and Acquisition of Legal Personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) administered by the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon electronic entry in the Zug Commercial Register, the registry transmits the registration data ex officio to SHAB for mandatory publication; the publication notice contains firm name, legal form, registered office, purpose, share capital, officers and signatory powers; verify the company's UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) and the official abstract in Zefix, as third parties can rely on the published fact of incorporation from that date.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SHAB publication is inaccurate or delayed, request a rectification notice from the Commercial Register Office; the register has a corrective publication duty; any third-party loss caused by defective publication can be claimed only against the register under applicable state liability rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Cantonal and Federal Tax, VAT and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Steueramt Kanton Zug (Cantonal Tax Office), Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC), and SVA Zug for social insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The cantonal tax authority automatically assesses the company for corporate income and capital tax upon Commercial Register entry; submit e-VAT registration to the ESTV if taxable turnover from colocation leases is expected to exceed CHF 100,000 within twelve months; obtain the UID/VAT number and agree the VAT accounting method; register with SVA Zug for AHV/AVS social insurance before the first employee is engaged, and notify the compensation fund for maternity and salary continuance obligations.
required_dossiers: VAT registration form (e-VAT) with projected turnover figures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If UID/VAT activation is delayed, address the ESTV Form 754.60 to the VAT helpline and submit a formal reminder with the registry extract; tax obligations are not suspended by administrative delay, so record pre-registration invoices carefully and reconcile the VAT start date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Building, Environmental, Fire and Occupational Licensing for the Data-Center Facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Baudirektion Kanton Zug (Building and Construction Directorate), Amt für Umwelt des Kantons Zug (Cantonal Environmental Office), Feuerpolizei Zug (Fire Inspectorate), and SUVA (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before fitting out the colocation halls, submit the building and operating permit application with layout drawings, raised-floor structural loads, UPS/battery rooms, cooling systems, emergency diesel generators, fire compartments and evacuation concept; secure the preliminary environmental screening under Art. 10a of the Swiss Environmental Protection Act and any wastewater discharge authorization; obtain the fire clearance and SUVA occupational safety assessment; commence construction only after the permit is final and any obligations on the EIA classification are incorporated into the operational plan.
required_dossiers: Site and floor layout plans with colocation hall zoning
Structural calculation report for racks, cooling plant and raised floors
Fire protection concept, gas suppression design and evacuation plan
Water discharge and cooling-tower water management plan
Diesel generator emission data per the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV/OAPC)
SUVA workplace safety and equipment clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is refused or conditioned, file an administrative objection with the Baudirektion within 30 days; a compliance program may be submitted to obtain a conditional operating permit, and further appeal lies to the Administrative Court of the Canton of Zug.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Baudirektion des Kantons Zug (Building and Spatial Development Directorate) acting with the Amt für Umwelt des Kantons Zug and the Feuerpolizei of Canton Zug; no federal sectoral concession is required for colocation leasing under ISIC 6209.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Construction and Operating Permit for a Tier-3/Tier-4 Data Center (Baubewilligung und Betriebsbewilligung) under cantonal building law and the Swiss Environmental Protection Act, encompassing commissioning of server halls, cooling plant, emergency power supply and associated technical infrastructure.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Amt für Umwelt des Kantons Zug (Environmental Protection Office of Canton Zug) in coordination with the Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Preliminary environmental screening / registration category under Art. 10a EPA and Annex to the Swiss EIA Ordinance (UVPV/OEIE); a full EIA report is triggered only where backup power installations exceed 20 MW thermal input or the site lies in an environmentally sensitive zone, with most typical colocation facilities being assessed through a self-declaration and site-specific screening.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater effluent must comply with the Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV/OEaux) and municipal sewer regulations, with pH 6.5-9, temperature not exceeding 30°C at the point of discharge, and COD/BOD concentrations within the local sewer bylaw limits; cooling-tower water cycles must be managed to prevent legionella and discharge blowdown under permit; emergency diesel-generator emissions must meet the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV/OAPC) threshold values for NOx and particulate matter, with VOC control for backup fuel storage; HVAC refrigerants must comply with the Swiss Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance for ozone-depleting and fluorinated greenhouse gases; spill containment and retention basins are mandatory for lubricants, battery electrolytes and fuel.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Feuerpolizei Kanton Zug verifying fire compartments, emergency exit distances, early-warning fire detection, N2/Argon gas suppression systems, and smoke extraction; structural load inspection and seismic compliance per SIA 261 for raised floors and plant rooms; SUVA occupational clearance covering confined-space entry, electrical safety on live UPS systems, battery rooms with gas detection, and lifting equipment; civil-defense compliance in Canton Zug satisfied through shelter construction of approximately 33% of above-grade floor area or payment of the statutory monetary compensation (Ersatzbeitrag) where shelter construction is technically impracticable for a data-center layout.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC); portal: www.estv.admin.ch (VAT e-services), www.uid.admin.ch (central UID register); cantonal tax administrations handle cantonal and communal direct taxes; Federal Customs Administration (Oberzolldirektion OZD / Federal Customs Administration FCA) operates the customs export/import procedure (e-dec / Passar).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft obtains its statutory business identifier UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, format CHE-###.###.###) automatically upon entry in the cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregister) after notarial incorporation; no separate TIN application is required. The Commercial Register notification triggers the cantonal direct tax assessment file. For VAT, the AG must file a VAT registration declaration with the ESTV/AFC through the VAT e-portal within 60 days after the end of the calendar year in which worldwide taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 (Art. 10, 11, 66 MWSTG); the ESTV then issues the VAT number CHE-###.###.### MWST. Foreign non-resident entities with Swiss-source taxable supplies exceeding CHF 100,000 must use the simplified non-established-person registration procedure via the ESTV and may be required to appoint a Swiss tax representative; alternatively, a foreign entity that is not required to register may claim input VAT refunds through the reciprocal Form 15 EUR procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the Swiss AG is resident in Switzerland, has unlimited tax liability on worldwide profits (Art. 50 DBG/LIFD), and is additionally subject to cantonal and communal corporate income tax and capital tax; there is no check-the-box or flow-through/transparent regime under Swiss law. The combined federal, cantonal and communal profit tax rate ranges from approximately 11.6% to 21% depending on canton; the federal portion is a flat 8.5% on net profit (effective federal rate approx. 7.8% after deduction of cantonal tax, itself tax-deductible). Distributions and interest to shareholders attract 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) subject to treaty relief, whereas operating rentals for colocation services fall outside the withholding tax net. For VAT, the AG is a taxable person (Art. 10 MWSTG) and supplies of data centre colocation services are standard-rated at 8.1% unless a zero-rating or out-of-scope place-of-supply rule applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists. Available statutory elections include: (i) voluntary VAT registration (opt-in) for a taxable person below the CHF 100,000 threshold, and voluntary VAT group registration (Unternehmensgruppe, Art. 21 MWSTG) among Swiss entities forming an integrated enterprise; (ii) election between the effective input-tax deduction method and the simplified apportioned-rate method (Saldosteuersatz, Art. 37 MWSTG) for taxpayers below the applicable turnover ceilings; (iii) the place-of-supply declaration under Art. 18(2)(b) MWSTG, under which a supplier of cross-border services may subject to Swiss VAT services that are effectively used or exploited in Switzerland in order to preserve input-VAT recovery, while services supplied to a foreign business recipient qualify for zero-rating under Art. 23(2) MWSTG if the foreign-status evidence is complete; (iv) for federal direct tax, elections relating to the participation exemption (Beteiligungsabzug, Art. 69 DBG), the R&D super-deduction, patent box, and notional interest deduction introduced by the 2020 Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (STAF/WEF 2020). Swiss law does not provide corporate income tax consolidation or fiscal unity for direct tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA), governed by the Federal Act on Value Added Tax of 12 June 2009 (MWSTG/LTVA) and the VAT Ordinance (MWSTV/OTVA); rates since 1 January 2024 are 8.1% standard, 2.6% reduced (food, books, pharmaceuticals), and 3.8% accommodation; the 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) applies to dividends and interest but not to operating lease/rental income from colocation services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies of goods and services (Art. 10 and 11 MWSTG); non-established foreign entities count Swiss-source turnover only; mandatory registration applies from the moment the threshold is exceeded, with a notification deadline of 60 days after the end of the relevant calendar year; voluntary registration is available to all taxable persons, and a VAT group can be registered where a parent and its Swiss group companies form a financially, economically, and organisationally integrated enterprise.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous-transmission, or digital stamping mandate comparable to Italy or Latin American regimes. E-invoicing is voluntary and market-driven, with Swiss eBill (SIX), Peppol BIS, and ZUGFeRD/Factur-X formats accepted. Mandatory invoice elements are set by Art. 26 MWSTG and include supplier UID/VAT number, recipient UID/VAT number, supply date, description, consideration, tax rate, and tax amount; simplified invoices with fewer elements are lawful below CHF 400. Since 1 January 2022, domestic invoices must carry the QR-invoice (SwissQR) payment slip, but this is a payment standard, not a fiscal-clearance mechanism. For zero-rated exports, the exporter must retain the invoice and a complete evidence set; foreign business recipients may be identified by their foreign VAT/UID number rather than a Swiss UID.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (tax-free with full input-VAT deduction, Art. 23 MWSTG) applies to: (a) goods physically exported from Switzerland, evidenced by a customs export declaration; and (b) services supplied to a recipient with its seat or residence abroad, provided the service is qualified as a business-to-business supply under Art. 18(2) MWSTG and is not effectively used or exploited in Switzerland. For data centre colocation, the Federal Tax Administration treats server housing as a service connected to movable tangible property located in Switzerland; therefore the supply occurs where the server is situated. A Swiss AG may invoice a foreign colocation customer at the zero rate only if it can prove: the customer is an entrepreneur or legal person with a foreign seat and no Swiss permanent establishment; the service is supplied for the customer's foreign business activity and is not used or exploited in Switzerland; and the external documentation (contract, foreign VAT/UID certificate, payment evidence) is conclusive at the time of invoicing. Where the foreign customer uses the service in Switzerland, the supply remains subject to Swiss VAT and the supplier may elect Swiss taxation to secure input-tax recovery; otherwise, services outside scope under the recipient-location rule need no Swiss VAT charge but still require equivalent proof. Import VAT and reverse-charge obligations are administered by the Federal Customs Administration; the EU OSS/MOSS regimes do not apply in Switzerland.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration issued via the e-dec / Passar procedure, including the customs tariff number, gross weight, statistical value, and the export-license or leaving certificate where applicable
Commercial invoice containing the mandatory Art. 26 MWSTG data elements, the applicable legal basis for zero-rating, and the currency and incoterms of the export supply
Transport document evidencing physical departure from Switzerland: CMR waybill, airway bill (AWB/IATA), or bill of lading, issued within the statutory export period
Customs or carrier evidence of arrival of the goods in the foreign destination country (customs entry or arrival stamp) for tangible goods exports

Written colocation or bare-metal hosting contract with the foreign customer specifying the place of consumption, the technical service scope (rack space, power, cooling, cross-connects, remote hands), and the Swiss infrastructure location

Certificate of the foreign customer's statutory business registration, such as a foreign VAT ID, USt-IdNr., BEVAT number, OSS VAT ID, or chamber-of-commerce extract, together with a declaration that the customer has no Swiss permanent establishment
Bank payment evidence or Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT MT103, credit advice) showing receipt of the export consideration from the foreign customer within the documented payment term
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The export evidence bundle must be retained for at least 10 years (Art. 32 and 58 MWSTG; commercial records), and the export evidence must be complete, consistent, and conclusive already at the time of invoicing. Incorrect or fraudulent zero-rating triggers retroactive VAT assessment at the standard rate of 8.1% on the gross consideration, plus default interest at 5% per annum (Art. 27, 30 and 32 MWSTG). Administrative fines for intentional tax evasion reach up to four times the evaded tax, capped at CHF 800,000 (Art. 70 MWSTG); disciplinary fines of up to CHF 10,000 apply for procedural breaches (Art. 72 MWSTG); wilful tax fraud is a criminal offence carrying imprisonment of up to five years (Art. 78 MWSTG). The taxpayer additionally loses the corresponding input-VAT deduction, and the foreign customer may face local reverse-charge assessments. Switzerland imposes no exchange-control or statutory FX-repatriation deadline; the 180-day term in compliance practice serves as the evidentiary ceiling for receiving and substantiating export consideration and aligning arm's-length transfer-pricing documentation. If the consideration is not repatriated within that period without adequate justification, the payment may be recharacterised as shareholder support or a constructive dividend subject to the 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Art. 4 and 13 VStG), together with interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank, including operational oversight of Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) and EuroSIC clearing railways.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland operates a fully liberalised and convertible currency regime. The Swiss franc (CHF) is fully convertible for both current-account transactions (goods, services, royalties, leases) and capital-account transactions (equity, shareholder debt, dividends, liquidation proceeds) under the Federal Act on Currency and Means of Payment (WZG). There are no capital controls, no foreign-exchange licensing requirements, and no prior SNB approval is required for cross-border capital movements or profit remittance by a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft. The only statutory levy on outbound dividends is the 35% Swiss federal withholding tax, which is recoverable or reduced under an applicable double taxation treaty or the notification procedure for qualifying corporate shareholders; automatic exchange of information (AEOI) reporting applies. For a data-centre colocation business, contracts may be freely denominated in CHF, EUR, or USD, and no restriction is imposed on the collection of cross-border colocation fees.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory repatriation timeline under Swiss monetary law. Colocation and service export receipts may be retained in any fully convertible currency in either domestic or foreign bank accounts. For balance-of-payments statistics only, the SNB aggregates bank reporting; no individual company filing, conversion mandate, or surrender deadline applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow account (Sperrkonto) and operational multi-currency account (CHF/EUR/USD) with SIC, EuroSIC and SWIFT access
Capital escrow account (Sperrkonto) and operational account with SIC, EuroSIC and SEPA direct-debit capabilities
Operational CHF/EUR account and capital escrow account (recommended where the data-centre premises are located in the Canton of Vaud)
Operational account with SIC and SEPA rails; capital escrow available at selected regional Raiffeisen banks

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for core treasury use. Offshore EU/UK-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) cannot issue a Swiss CH-IBAN, lack access to SIC/EuroSIC settlement, and cannot satisfy the statutory blocked deposit verification required for the AG minimum share capital. FINMA-authorised fintech banks holding a FinTech licence under Article 1b of the Swiss Banking Act (public-deposit cap of CHF 100 million), such as Neon or Yapeal, may serve only as secondary accounts for low-value recurring tenant-fee collections; they generally do not offer documentary letters of credit, FX hedging, or same-day CHF clearing. The legal constraint under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) and banking practice is that the capital escrow and primary liquidity rails must be held with a FINMA-supervised bank participating in Swiss clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is conditionally permitted: under FINMA Circular 2016/07, Swiss banks may rely on an approved electronic identity-verification process (video or certified e-ID) in lieu of a face-to-face interview. In practice, UBS, ZKB, and the cantonal banks require at least one authorised director or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) to attend a physical KYC meeting in Switzerland, or to complete identity verification at a Swiss embassy or certifying notary, whenever the shareholders are non-resident. The company should appoint a Swiss-resident authorised signatory (even with limited proxy) to satisfy the bank's substance expectations. A physical interview is categorically mandatory if the UBO is resident in a FATF-listed jurisdiction or qualifies as a politically exposed person (PEP).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital-injection red flag: the CHF 100,000 share capital is funded from an offshore or third-party account, or the UBO cannot demonstrate an auditable source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies of the UBO and directors; 3 to 6 months of bank statements evidencing the source of funds; group structure chart; capital deposit confirmation (Einzahlungsbestätigung) issued by the Swiss bank on the blocked Sperrkonto; and the commercial register application (B-card) identifying the paid-up capital amount.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto-adjacent activity: tenants or counterparties linked to Zug's Crypto Valley, digital-asset exchanges, or token issuers triggering enhanced due diligence under FINMA Circular 2020/02.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A fiat-only treasury policy confirming that no cryptocurrency flows through the bank accounts; complete tenant due-diligence files with executed colocation contracts and rack/power SLAs; and an AML risk self-assessment demonstrating that the company is a physical infrastructure lessor rather than a virtual-asset service provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance red flag: a newly incorporated AG with no office, no staff, no financial statements, or a mere virtual-office address, indicating a shell-company pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed lease agreement for the data-centre facility; Swiss payroll records and AHV social-security declarations where employees are engaged; pro-forma financial statements; Swiss VAT registration confirmation (CHE-number); and a detailed business plan with forecast colocation capacity utilisation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through liquidity red flag: monthly inflows from multiple unrelated tenant colocation payments are misread as money remittance, fund pass-through, or an unlicensed payment-services business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master service agreements with each tenant specifying the leased racks, bandwidth, and power circuits; corresponding commercial invoices describing colocation services; SLAs and incident reports; and a written treasury mandate confirming the company does not act as a payment intermediary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The initial equity contribution (minimum nominal CHF 100,000, of which at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up and freely at the disposal of the board) must be credited to the bank's segregated blocked capital account (Sperrkonto). Routing: SWIFT MT103, or an internal Swiss payment via SIC for domestic shareholders, with ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (equity-like capital) or 'COST' (capital contribution); the remitter must be the subscribing shareholder, never a third party. The commercial register requires the bank's capital deposit certificate (Einzahlungsbestätigung / Attestation de libération) before registration is finalised. Subsequent shareholder loans must be routed via MT103 with purpose code 'LEND' or 'INTC', supported by a written shareholder-loan agreement at arm's-length interest, and are governed by the capital-liability provisions of the Swiss Code of Obligations (Articles 632 et seq.).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing-rail matrix: (i) domestic CHF disbursements via SIC real-time final settlement; (ii) EUR payments within the SEPA zone, including Switzerland as a SEPA participating country, via SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Direct Debit (Core or B2B scheme) for recurring monthly tenant collections, cleared through EuroSIC; (iii) non-SEPA cross-border payments via SWIFT MT103 with ISO 20022 purpose codes referencing the underlying colocation or service invoice; (iv) high-value data-centre hardware imports (servers, cooling, and power infrastructure exceeding CHF 100,000 equivalent) through an irrevocable confirmed documentary Letter of Credit (UCP 600) or standby letter of credit payable at sight, settled via SWIFT; and (v) tax and social-security disbursements to Swiss authorities through the Swiss QR-bill (QR-IBAN) or SIC direct debit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (CHF/EUR, CHF/USD) up to 12-month tenor, executed under an ISDA or Swiss Master Agreement for OTC derivatives with the account-holding bank
FX swaps (tom-next, spot-forward, and forward-forward swaps) limited to balance-sheet liquidity management
Plain-vanilla European-style FX options (call and put) with a documented non-speculative hedging purpose and a bank credit-line limit
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) matched to the currency and interest profile of the data-centre facility loan or capital lease
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only as a hedge for the exotic counterparty-currency leg of a commercial contract; not market-standard for CHF because the Swiss franc is fully convertible

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal and Cantonal Corporate Income Tax Return (Steuererklärung juristische Personen) filed jointly with audited annual financial statements (Jahresrechnung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) as single point of receipt; Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) receives the federal direct tax share
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due within 3 months of the balance-sheet date; for a 31 December year-end the standard cantonal deadline is 31 March of the following year, with routinely granted extensions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquency interest at 5% p.a. on assessed federal/cantonal tax from the contractual due date; procedural fines for late or incomplete filing up to CHF 10,000 per Art. 174 DBG; no administrative strike-off is available under Swiss law for tax non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quarterly Swiss VAT Return (MWST-Abrechnung) with final annual reconciliation of the reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Main Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the end of each quarter (Q1 due approx. 30 May; Q2 approx. 30 Aug; Q3 approx. 30 Nov; Q4 approx. 28/29 Feb of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 5% p.a.; procedural fines for non-filing or incorrect returns up to CHF 3,000 (ordinary) and up to CHF 30,000 in aggravated cases per Arts. 70–72 MWSTG; persistent default may trigger debt-collection enforcement (Betreibungsverfahren)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Employer Social Security Wage Declaration (AHV-Lohnmeldung) covering all salaried staff of the colocation operation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Fund (Ausgleichskasse) of the registered seat
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 January of the calendar year following the wage-payment year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines (Ordnungsbusse) up to CHF 5,000 plus retroactive assessment of unpaid social security contributions with default interest

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register and beneficial-ownership review (internal corporate housekeeping; Switzerland imposes no annual return or franchise filing to the Commercial Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors (Art. 716a OR); qualified statutory auditor where an ordinary or limited audit is applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at the board meeting approving the annual financial statements and no later than 6 months after balance-sheet date; immediate updating upon share transfers or changes in effective control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Board criminal liability for deficient registers under Art. 697p OR (fine up to CHF 5,000); where the AG ceases to maintain a valid board or registered office, the Commercial Register may obtain a judicial liquidation order under Art. 731b OR

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit by a Swiss licensed audit firm is mandatory where two of the following three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: total assets above CHF 20,000,000, annual turnover above CHF 40,000,000, average headcount above 250 FTE (Art. 727a OR). Qualified audit exemption ('limited audit') applies below these thresholds; full opt-out from external audit is available only via unanimous shareholder resolution and only if the company is not subject to ordinary audit and maintains no controlling interests (Art. 727 OR).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Jahresrechnung, Arts. 957–963b OR) with Swiss GAAP FER as the primary local standard; IFRS is permitted for the annual or consolidated financial statements. True-and-fair presentation and the going-concern principle apply under Art. 960 OR.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Swiss AG is not subject to an annual public UBO filing. The company must maintain an internal register of beneficial owners under Art. 697j OR recording every natural person who directly or indirectly holds at least 25% of capital or voting rights or otherwise controls the AG. The register must be reviewed, updated and signed at least annually by the board when approving the financial statements; any share-triggered change is recorded immediately. Knowingly false or incomplete records are criminally sanctioned (Art. 697p OR).
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (Register der wirtschaftlich Berechtigten, Art. 697j OR)
Board of Directors' Minute Book (Verwaltungsratsprotokoll, Art. 713 OR)
Shareholders' Meeting Minute Book (Generalversammlungsprotokoll, Art. 702 OR)
Accounting books, vouchers and annual reports (Art. 958f OR)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,000–6,500 per annum for a licensed Swiss corporate agent or business-address fiduciary service covering legal mailing services and postal handling; owner-occupied premises incur only municipal property tax with no statutory annual corporate fee
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 18,000–55,000 per annum for a full ordinary audit of a data-center balance sheet above the Art. 727a OR thresholds; USD 8,000–20,000 per annum for a limited statutory audit where exemption thresholds are not exceeded

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal statutory corporate income tax (effective federal rate 7.83% after deductibility of the federal tax itself); cantonal/communal corporate income taxes are added on taxable profit and vary between approximately 10.75% (Zug) and 24.80% (Geneva), producing an aggregate headline rate range of roughly 11.9% to 21.1% for benchmark cantons such as Zug and Zurich.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory reduction instruments following TRAF (Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act 2020): (1) cantonal patent box exempting up to 90% of qualifying IP-derived net income; (2) super-deduction of 50% of qualifying domestic R&D labour costs; (3) federal and cantonal participation relief fully exempting substantiated dividend income and capital gains on qualifying holdings (10% or more, or acquisition cost exceeding CHF 1,000,000); (4) optional notional interest deduction on excess equity in implementing cantons; (5) accelerated tax depreciation on server hardware, cabling, cooling equipment and leasehold improvements of a Tier-3/4 data centre, which can materially lower the effective rate below the statutory headline in early operating years.
